findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When a slot's date has an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy times. An override defines working availability, not an exemption from existing bookings or calendar conflicts. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be shown as available during an existing meeting on an override date. Validate the override window and then continue through the busy-time checks.

findings.title: Override validation accepts slots only partially inside availability
findings.body: The override checks reject slots ending at or before the override start and slots starting after its end, but do not require the whole slot to fit inside the override. For example, a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 slot generated by a round-robin host. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end for at least one override interval.

findings.title: Split working hours reject slots inside valid intervals
findings.body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits inside at least one interval. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected by the morning interval. This newly added check removes valid availability for ordinary split-day schedules. Check for containment in an applicable interval, using the slot end time rather than the slot start for the end boundary.

findings.title: Timezone conversion discards date changes at midnight
findings.body: The converted override boundaries are reduced to hour/minute values without preserving a day rollover, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override start date. For example, a UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+3 becomes 01:00–02:00 but is inserted into the original attendee date instead of the following date. An interval crossing attendee midnight can also produce startTime > endTime and disappear entirely. Convert the full override interval to attendee time, select it by overlap with the attendee day, and clip or split it at day boundaries before extracting minutes.
